findings.title: Local fallback does not revoke an existing federated recovery credential
findings.body: If a user-storage provider exposes an existing recovery credential but returns `false` from `updateCredential` (for example, because it is read-only), this branch creates a local replacement without removing or disabling the federated credential. The federated credential remains usable for authentication, and `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` prefers it over the new local credential. Consequently, reconfiguring recovery codes does not revoke the old codes and may leave the newly generated credential masked.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed
findings.body: This validator returns true for a matching recovery code but never removes or marks that code as used in `myUser.recoveryCodes`. The same code can therefore authenticate repeatedly in this user-storage implementation, unlike a one-time recovery code. The new integration test uses each code only once, so it passes without detecting this behavior; update the stored credential on successful validation and test that reuse fails.
